codeReview.summary: Clean, well-structured implementation that faithfully adapts multi-agent mission system createSalientSummarySchema pattern to Flywheel's WorkerHandoffSchema. The countSentences helper is a near-verbatim port of reference sentence counting logic. The WorkerHandoffBaseSchema / WorkerHandoffSchema split is a smart architectural choice that enables .pick()/.omit() projections (used by EvaluatorHandoffDataSchema) while keeping cross-field superRefine checks on the full validation path. All six expectedBehavior items are covered with 26 new tests. Error messages are self-correcting with field name, constraint, and fix instruction. The evaluator.ts change to use WorkerHandoffBaseSchema.pick() instead of WorkerHandoffSchema.pick() is correct and well-documented with a comment explaining why cross-field refinements don't apply to projections.

issues.description:
The reference createSalientSummarySchema also checks for  via .includes(''), but the Flywheel implementation already handles this correctly in the refine callback: `!s.includes('
') && !s.includes('')`. However, the reference error message says 'no newlines' while Flywheel's says 'newline characters (
 or 
)' — the Flywheel version is more helpful. No action needed, just noting the divergence is intentional and beneficial.

SUMMARY_MAX_LENGTH is 5000 vs reference implementation's 750 (handoff) / 500 (compact). This is intentional since Flywheel's summary field serves a broader purpose than the reference salientSummary. The constants are well-named and centralized at the top of the schema section, making future tuning straightforward.

The '0 sentences' test uses a string of spaces ('                              ') which passes min(20) but fails the sentence count check. This is a reasonable edge case test, though it's somewhat indirect — the spaces pass min-length but get trimmed to empty by countSentences. The behavior is correct but could be more explicitly documented in the test name (e.g., 'rejects whitespace-only summary that passes length check').

sharedStateObservations.observation: The worker introduced a WorkerHandoffBaseSchema / WorkerHandoffSchema split pattern to support .pick()/.omit() on the base z.object while keeping superRefine cross-field checks separate. This is a reusable pattern for any Zod schema that needs both projections and cross-field validation. The architecture.md library file doesn't mention this pattern yet.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/schemas/handoff.ts:118-155 — WorkerHandoffBaseSchema (z.object) exported for projections, WorkerHandoffSchema = WorkerHandoffBaseSchema.superRefine(...) for full validation. src/schemas/evaluator.ts:11 now imports WorkerHandoffBaseSchema instead of WorkerHandoffSchema.

summary: Pass. The implementation faithfully ports the multi-agent mission system createSalientSummarySchema pattern with improvements (more descriptive error messages, explicit \r handling). The WorkerHandoffBaseSchema split cleanly solves the .pick() compatibility issue with superRefine. All 6 expectedBehavior items are satisfied with 26 comprehensive tests. The evaluator.ts update is correct. No blocking issues found. Three non-blocking observations noted: intentional divergence from reference error messages (beneficial), higher max length (intentional), and a minor test naming suggestion.
